benchmark: Fakeddit real Reddit image-text subset (community mirror)

dataset.label_definition: Source six-way label 0 (true) maps to REAL; labels 1-5 (satire, false connection, imposter, manipulated, misleading content) map to FAKE. Labels are inherited distant supervision, not new fact-checks or image-authenticity annotations.

limitations: Only supplied source identifiers and hashes are audited; unidentified related events and near-duplicate images can remain.
Overlap with the frozen encoder's undisclosed pretraining corpus cannot be ruled out.
Community mirror lacks a dataset card, original Reddit post IDs and documented sampling/split provenance.
Fakeddit labels are distant supervision from subreddit categories, not independent fact-checks for every post.
FAKE includes satire, false connections, imposter, manipulated and misleading content; REAL means source label true, not a new truth verification.
Image/text exact duplicates are audited, but near-duplicate events and pretraining overlap are not ruled out.
Only supplied source identifiers and hashes are audited; unidentified related events and near-duplicate images can remain.
Overlap with the frozen encoder's undisclosed pretraining corpus cannot be ruled out.
This is a subset/mirror evaluation unless the dataset manifest explicitly establishes otherwise; full published benchmark performance is not claimed.
Dataset labels may reflect weak supervision or source conventions; the classifier does not establish real-world truth.
The image branch uses frozen CLIP vision features; the text branch is a separate train-fitted TF-IDF plus logistic regression model.
Scores are uncalibrated dataset class estimates; arbitrary uploads have not been validated as in-domain.
No real-world face-swap, synthetic speech, video, human explanation, or external-domain evaluation was performed.

provenance.split_origin: Community mirror; original paper split provenance unverified

experiments.name: Text-only baseline
experiments.description: L2 logistic regression on train-fitted TF-IDF word and bigram features.

experiments.name: Image-only baseline
experiments.description: L2 logistic regression on frozen normalized CLIP image embeddings.

experiments.name: Feature-level fusion
experiments.description: L2 logistic regression on concatenated CLIP image and TF-IDF text features.

experiments.name: Decision-level fusion
experiments.description: Independent image/text head probabilities blended by validation-selected weight.

experiments.name: Modality ablation
experiments.description: Inference ablation of the trained fusion model using training means; this intervention is outside the original input distribution.

variants.name: Without Text
variants.description: Replace the removed modality and its joint features with training means; no retraining.

variants.name: Without Image
variants.description: Replace the removed modality and its joint features with training means; no retraining.

experiments.name: External-domain evaluation
experiments.description: Not evaluated: this run has no independently held-out source domain or deepfake benchmark.

majority_baseline.name: Training-majority baseline
majority_baseline.description: Always predict the most frequent training label. The test distribution is not used to choose the class.

training.head: L2 logistic regression
training.text_model: train-fitted TF-IDF unigram/bigram features with L2 logistic regression

models.selection: Lowest validation log loss among the four models; test labels unused for selection.
models.score_meaning: Uncalibrated probability estimate for the dataset's FAKE label.

encoder.timing_scope: Wall time for this extraction invocation including cache lookup and model loading; earlier interrupted invocations are excluded.
encoder.cache_key_inputs: encoder files + image file bytes / exact caption text; no labels or split names
encoder.extraction: local CLIP image/text encoders on supplied natural-media files
limitations: Input-to-embedding correspondence is supplied by the embedding provider and has not been independently re-encoded.
